LESSON: STORY TELLING LISTENING

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Story Telling LISTENING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Story Telling LISTENING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: When are stories respond to stories peers, teacher, a resource person(if told?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use a variety of thematic vocabulary available), audio recorded stories
2. appreciate their culture and values as  Learners respond to oral questions taught through oral stories related to the story learned or orally

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: STORY TELLING LISTENING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Story Telling LISTENING helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: STORY TELLING LISTENING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use a variety of thematic vocabulary available), audio recorded stories

What this means
In this part you learn to use a variety of thematic vocabulary available), audio recorded stories. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use a variety of thematic vocabulary available), audio recorded stories.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Story Telling LISTENING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use a variety of thematic vocabulary available), audio recorded stories. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate their culture and values as  Learners respond to oral questions taught through oral stories related to the story learned or orally

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate their culture and values as  Learners respond to oral questions taught through oral stories related to the story learned or orally. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate their culture and values as  Learners respond to oral questions taught through oral stories related to the story learned or orally.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Story Telling LISTENING to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate their culture and values as  Learners respond to oral questions taught through oral stories related to the story learned or orally. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Story Telling LISTENING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Story Telling LISTENING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use a variety of thematic vocabulary available), audio recorded stories)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Story Telling LISTENING to a partner. (skill: appreciate their culture and values as  Learners respond to oral questions taught through oral stories related to the story learned or orally)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Story Telling LISTENING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use a variety of thematic vocabulary available), audio recorded stories.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate their culture and values as  Learners respond to oral questions taught through oral stories related to the story learned or orally.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Story Telling LISTENING from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Story Telling LISTENING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Story Telling LISTENING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When are stories respond to stories peers, teacher, a resource person(if told?
2. What do stories c) develop an interest in listening to oral  Learners record their stories and listen teach us?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Story Telling LISTENING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use a variety of thematic vocabulary available), audio recorded stories.
5. Be able to: appreciate their culture and values as  Learners respond to oral questions taught through oral stories related to the story learned or orally.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
